Fitter API

This is the highest level module that handles the fitting procedure

inverse_thomson_scattering.fitter.init_param_norm_and_shift(config: Dict) → DictSource

Initializes the dictionary that contains the normalization constants for all the parameters

The parameters are all normalized from 0 to 1 in order to improve gradient flow

Parameters:

config – Dict

Returns: Dict

inverse_thomson_scattering.fitter._validate_inputs_(config: Dict) → DictSource

This function adds derived configuration quantities that are necessary for the fitting process

Parameters:

config – Dict

Returns: Dict

inverse_thomson_scattering.fitter.scipy_angular_loop(config: Dict, all_data: Dict, sa) → Tuple[Dict, float, TSFitter]Source

Performs angular thomson scattering i.e. ARTEMIS fitting exercise using the SciPy optimizer routines

Parameters:

  • config

  • all_data

  • best_weights

  • all_weights

  • sa

Returns:

inverse_thomson_scattering.fitter.angular_adam(config, all_data, sa, batch_indices, num_batches)Source

This performs an SGD-like fitting routine. It is different than the SciPy routines primarily because we have to manage the number of iterations manually whereas the SciPy routines have their own convergence/termination process

Parameters:

  • config

  • all_data

  • sa

  • batch_indices

  • num_batches

Returns:

inverse_thomson_scattering.fitter.one_d_loop(config: Dict, all_data: Dict, sa: Tuple, batch_indices: ndarray, num_batches: int) → Tuple[List, float, TSFitter]Source

This is the higher level wrapper that prepares the data and the fitting code for the 1D fits

This function branches out into the various optimization routines for fitting.

For now, this is either running the ADAM loop or the SciPy optimizer loop

Parameters:

  • config

  • all_data

  • sa

  • batch_indices

  • num_batches

Returns:

inverse_thomson_scattering.fitter.fit(config) → Tuple[DataFrame, float]Source

This function fits the Thomson scattering spectral density function to experimental data, or plots specified spectra. All inputs are derived from the input dictionary config.

Summary of additional needs:

A wrapper to allow for multiple lineouts or shots to be analyzed and gradients to be handled Better way to handle data finding since the location may change with computer or on a shot day Better way to handle shots with multiple types of data Way to handle calibrations which change from one to shot day to the next and have to be recalculated frequently (adding a new function to attempt this 8/8/22) A way to handle the expanded ion calculation when colapsing the spectrum to pixel resolution A way to handle different numbers of points

Depreciated functions that need to be restored:

Time axis alignment with fiducials interactive confirmation of new table creation ability to generate different table names without the default values

Parameters:

config

Returns:
